what: The working real-arm Dream path is Dream's own station (dreamcli setup / dreamcli robot, the robots package in dreamlabs 1.0.37), which the Windows/WSL laptop runs; DreamSim/dream_arm.py is not equivalent and stays a guarded experiment.
why: The station is a port of MakerMods' reference Maker Arm driver: a 20 Hz control loop that keeps refilling Dream's 48-row chunks while the arm moves and commands both arms at 250 Hz between rows. dream_arm.py played one row per chunk through pickup_server's blocking 15 deg/s moves, so Dream drove a far slower, stop-start robot than it plans for.
details: The station opens a candleLight adapter only as a Linux SocketCAN link (kernel gs_usb driver) or a CANable on slcan firmware; its raw-USB candleLight transport is not ported, so it cannot drive these adapters from macOS. That is why it runs under WSL on Windows.

Jetson (L4T R39.2.1, kernel 6.8.12-1021-tegra): CONFIG_CAN and CAN_RAW are modules but CONFIG_CAN_GS_USB is not set; kernel headers are installed, so gs_usb can be built out of tree to run the station there.
Maker Arm motor temperature limits are set in the station with `dreamcli robot temp --warn/--stop`.
